newsitem.title: GERMANY: Klima says Austria to qualify for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Klima says Austria to qualify for EMU.

text.p: Austrian Chancellor Viktor Klima was quoted on Tuesday as saying Vienna would meet the Maastricht treaty deficit target of three percent of GDP this year to qualify for European monetary union (EMU) in 1999.

Klima, who visits Bonn on Wednesday, also told the weekly Die Zeit that a delay to EMU would be counter-productive. Omitting Germany from the starting lineup due to Bonn's budget difficulties was "not a realistic option", he said.
Klima said "in 1997, we will limit our total public sector deficit to three percent of gross domestic product (GDP)."

Asked whether the launch of the single currency should be delayed if Germany, troubled by record post-war unemployment, failed to meet the three percent target this year, he said that such a delay would last at least 10 years.

EMU without Germany would not make any sense either since countries like Austria and the Netherlands, who have for years linked their currencies to the German mark, could suffer consequences "which I cannot even imagine," he said.

The chancellor also said he supported a reading of the Maastricht Treaty which allowed, for example, public debt to exceed the reference value of 60 percent of GDP as long as the debt is falling continuously.

"Austria, for example, will in all probability not achieve 60 percent but already in 1997 and in following years, will be able to demonstrate a continous fall in the debt quota in that direction," he told Die Zeit.
